== Biography ==
Andrew is associated with the child christened on 19 November 1714 at Kirknewton and East Calder, whose father was also named Andrew Glasgow. His exact birth date is not established.<ref>https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-NV9</ref> His probable father is [[Glasgow-1546|Andrew Glasgow]] under the retained 85% assessment. [[Cook-36136|Christian Cook]] is the inherited mother reference, whose identity and maternity remain unassessed. An earlier draft linked Andrew Glasgow-1334; that superseded identifier is retained here as history rather than the selected father.
== Research Notes ==
=== Birth date and 1714 christening ===

The full [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-NV9 FamilySearch transcript] records Andrew Glasgow, son of Andrew Glasgow, christened on 19 November 1714 at Kirknewton and East Calder. Its Birth Date field displays only “11”. That fragment does not establish 11 November 1714 as his birthday. The earlier claim that he was born about 11 November 1714 remains an unproved interpretation of this source, distinct from its complete christening date. The transcript supplies no mother, residence, occupation or witnesses to distinguish the child from the later adult. The original register image remains restricted and uninspected. The existing family identifications and confidence assessments are unchanged.

=== Penicuik William: unresolved dates and identity ===

The Findmypast transcript of a Penicuik entry names William Glasgow, father Andrew Glasgow and mother Margaret Linton. It labels his birth 17 April 1745 and his baptism 17 April 1754.<ref name="PenicuikWilliam1754">Findmypast, Scotland, Parish Births &amp; Baptisms 1564-1929, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4602994 William Glasgow, SCOT/OPR/BAP/4602994], Penicuik, OPR 697/1, item 1, page 225; provider transcript inspected 30 October 2026; original register uninspected.</ref> Those dates allow a nine-year interval before baptism. The held evidence does not establish whether the interval is correct or whether a year has been transcribed incorrectly; neither date can yet be replaced.

[[Glasgow-1336|Andrew Glasgow]] is a candidate for the named father, but the held records do not identify him with the Penicuik adult. His approximate generation is compatible with a child born in 1745. His documented comparison household with [[Clerk-314|Isobel Clerk]] includes [[Glasgow-1320|William]], baptised in 1739, [[Glasgow-1323|Jean]], baptised in 1743, and [[Glasgow-1321|Alexander]], baptised in 1747. That household does not establish a union with Margaret Linton. Isobel is not named in the Penicuik transcript and is not identified with Margaret. No additional spouse, child or mother is inferred. The 1739 William cannot also be the child literally born in 1745 unless a source discrepancy is resolved.

The useful next check is the wording and dates of the original Penicuik entry, with any traceable companion transcription. Repeated derivative entries would not be independent corroboration.

=== Parish household review, 23 October 2026 ===

[[Glasgow-1321|Alexander Glasgow]] → [[Glasgow-1336|Andrew Glasgow]]: 95% → 76% (probable). Alexander-1321 represents the documented 1774–1776 Edinburgh brewer’s-servant household with Agnes Cunningham. The 1747 Kirknewton baptism names Andrew Glasgow and Isobel Clerk; 95% remains the conditional assessment of that child’s parent clause. Age about 27 in 1774 and compatible regional chronology support identifying the child with the adult, but no held record connects the childhood to the later occupation or spouse. The full adult-to-Andrew-1336 placement is therefore 76%. The graph percentage assesses the complete adult-profile father proposition. The prior 95% concerned only the record-defined 1747 child and is preserved with that scope, not disproved. The 1751 Glasgow Alexander entry remains an unresolved comparison, not a demonstrated rival. No father is replaced and no vital field or mother is changed. Original register images uninspected.
